title: Conditional probabilities in quantum-optical settings
abstract: We examine conditional probabilities derived from the joint noisy measurement of two complementary observables. We show that conditioning on one variable can lead to reduction of uncertainty in the other one, even completely eliminating uncertainty. We show that the conditional distribution cannot, in general, be represented in Born form using the marginal positive operator valued measure and any physical system state, nor can it be derived from typical rules of state reduction. We examine these issues in two basic quantum-optical schemes. These are double homodyne detection and a qubit measurement.
summary: This paper examines how conditional probabilities are generated when performing joint noisy measurements on complementary observables in quantum optics. It demonstrates that while conditioning can drastically reduce uncertainty, the resulting statistics do not generally conform to standard rules of state reduction or Born formalism. This challenges fundamental assumptions about measurement theory in quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates conditional probabilities derived from joint noisy measurements of complementary observables, questioning whether these statistics adhere to standard quantum mechanical rules like Born form or typical state reduction.
main_result: The derived conditional probability distribution cannot, in general, be represented by a reduced state using the marginal POVM, indicating that the measurement process induces transformations not covered by standard state reduction rules.
method: The analysis uses Wigner function formalisms and Bayes' rule for Gaussian cases to calculate joint and conditional probabilities ($	ilde{p}(x|y)$) in quantum-optical settings.
model_or_system: Two primary quantum-optical schemes are analyzed: double homodyne detection (measuring quadratures $X$ and $Y$) and a qubit measurement using Pauli observables. The input state is often modeled as a squeezed vacuum state.
key_observables: Quadrature operators ($X, Y$), conditional variance ($\sigma_{x|y}$), and the joint probability distribution $	ilde{p}(x, y)$.
important_parameters: Squeezing factor ($r$), rotation angle ($	heta$), and measurement noise parameters ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The explicit calculations rely on assuming Gaussian system states for simplification in later sections.
figures_summary: Not specified by the notes, but the analysis involves comparing joint quantum statistics $	ilde{p}(x, y)$ with classical/semiclassical limits and demonstrating violations of uncertainty relations ($\sigma_{x|y} \ge \Sigma_{xx}$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the joint noisy measurement via a POVM to calculating the resulting joint statistics using Wigner functions. It then analyzes the conditional distribution, culminating in proofs showing its non-reproducibility by standard reduced state formalisms.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses foundational issues in quantum measurement theory and contextuality within the framework of continuous variable quantum optics, which is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems.
